title: Decision-level frozen-expert gate three-seed smoke
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: A low-capacity gate trained from full-hand returns across the six-policy broad league can learn when to mix a frozen alternate expert into Standard10 at individual decisions, while preserving at least 75% of Standard10 greedy actions and improving paired greedy outcomes across three SHA-disjoint holdout opponents, both seats, and multiple seeds.
material_change: Freeze Standard10 and diverse_league5 tensors. Train only a small gate on legal current-state observations and the two experts' detached action distributions, using balanced opponent-seat PPO updates from 4096 on-policy hands per each of three seeds. Evaluate every endpoint against Standard10 on 512 common decks per holdout opponent, both seats; no Slumbot data or benchmark-specific rule enters training.
baseline: Frozen Standard10 greedy under identical holdout opponent/deck/seat cells.
notes: Preregistered admission requires exact hand counts, finite nonzero gate gradients, endpoint alternate mean weight 1-50%, 0.5-25% greedy disagreement from Standard10, positive pooled paired delta, positive median seed delta, at least two of three seed deltas positive, all three holdout-opponent deltas positive, and both seat deltas positive. Passing is only admission to a geometric learned-gate curve, not external-strength evidence.

Initial run stopped before the first hand because legacy-v4 places physical b200 at slot3 while native-v6 places it at slot2. The legal physical-action sets and probabilities were valid. Recovery aligns detached alternate probabilities by physical action string into the Standard10 canonical table; a targeted permutation test was added. Empty run/ is preserved; recovery1 is fresh.

Recovery1 stopped before evidence/checkpoint output when a reachable state exposed different legal bet-size sets across legacy-v4 and native-v6. Recovery2 mixes detached distributions on an 18-wide physical-action union, preserving every expert probability and using engine-validated action strings. Added a distinct-action-set union test; run/ and recovery1/ remain preserved.

Two preserved preflights generated zero completed hands: run/ exposed the legacy/native min-raise slot permutation; recovery1/ exposed state-dependent legal bet-size set differences. Recovery2 aligned experts on an 18-wide physical-action union and completed cleanly. Five targeted tests and the full 304-test AlphaHoldem suite passed.

result.summary: Three independent decision-gate seeds completed exactly 12,288 on-policy training hands and 18,432 common-deck evaluation hands. Gradients were finite/nonzero and Standard10 preservation held (4.98% alternate weight, 0.831% greedy disagreement), but pooled paired delta was -2.03 bb/100 CI [-15.56,+11.51]; seed deltas were -0.69, -11.77, and +6.39, with only one positive seed and negative point deltas on two holdout opponents and both seats.
result.conclusion: The current low-dose gate is mechanically valid and preserves Standard10, but it does not establish broad reward improvement and must not be scaled. Because endpoint alternate weights remained essentially at the 5% initialization (4.974-4.998%), this rejects the current optimizer dose and frozen 5% mixture result, not a fully learned decision-level router or long-horizon training.
result.next_step: Before any new environment hands, audit exact initial-to-final gate parameter movement and output sensitivity from the three checkpoints. If updates are genuinely negligible, run at most one preregistered optimizer-dose calibration/rerun with saved transition evidence; require material gate movement plus multi-seed holdout direction before a geometric curve. Otherwise close the route.
